Traditional Damascene jewelry is characterized by the art of inlaying oxidized steel or darkened backgrounds with precious metals like 24K/18K gold and silver. This piece showcases a "renaissance" style variant of the craft, featuring ornate stars, floral motifs, and geometric lines popular throughout the mid-to-late 20th century. This specific design utilizes a distinctive two-tone finish where the center details mimic a textured silver relief set within a polished gold-tone framework. Authentic mid-century pieces originating from Toledo, Spain are highly collectible.

While the Jennings Brothers Manufacturing Company was founded in Bridgeport, Connecticut, they operated a major New York showroom and marked many of their Colonial Revival and Old Colony Pewter hollowware lines with J.B.N.Y. or J.B.-N.Y. • 80: This is a factory catalog or pattern number, not a year or purity percentage. Pewter manufacturers stamped two-, three-, or four-digit numbers onto the bases of dishes, bowls, pitchers, and shakers to track specific shapes and molds in their catalogs. Age & Background • Era: Pieces carrying the J.B.N.Y. stamp alongside GENUINE PEWTER generally date from the 1920s to the early 1950s (the company ceased operations in 1953, though some dies were later acquired by other makers). • Care Tip: Pewter is a very soft metal; avoid abrasive polishes or dishwashers, which can scratch the surface and wear down the stamped markings.
